prize_parts.citation: for the invention and realization of optical lattice clocks, trapping neutral atoms at a magic wavelength and bringing atomic timekeeping to the 10^-18 level

statement.case_for: After the full first-round exchange I keep B030 alone, credited to Katori and Ye, and my confidence has risen because the objections raised against it have been answered in the record rather than left open. As the chair's first question asks, here is the one sentence that separates it from the 2005 and 2012 prizes: the frequency comb gave the means to count optical cycles and the 2012 prize honoured control of single trapped quantum systems, whereas the lattice clock is the new idea of confining a large ensemble of neutral atoms at a magic wavelength so that the trap leaves the clock transition unperturbed, which joins ion-level accuracy to the statistics of many atoms. That is a different invention, proposed by Katori and taken to its limit in Ye's laboratory. The demonstrated result, fractional uncertainties near 1e-18 reproduced independently in Japan, the US and Europe, is exactly the verified-instrument standard I apply as an experimentalist. The case rests on demonstrated performance alone, not on the pending redefinition of the second, and I would write the citation around the magic-wavelength lattice, which is the scope Olsson and Mehlig also ask for. Seven of eight members now prefer this configuration, but I do not count that as the argument; the argument is the one above.
statement.case_against: The overlap with the 2005 and 2012 metrology prizes is still my strongest reservation. Mehlig is right that spectroscopy, cooling and trapping are close in method, and my one-sentence distinction answers the idea but cannot remove the optics of a third award in one lineage. The credit boundary is a judgement, not a clean fact: Lemonde, Lisdat, Ludlow and the ion-clock groups contributed to the accuracy records and sit outside the pair, and I cannot verify the exact credit shares from the supplied text. Finally, the redefinition of the second has not occurred, so the societal payoff remains anticipated. None of these three seems to me disqualifying, but they are the real cost of the choice and the committee should record them honestly.

responses.point: Mehlig does not treat the overlap with the 2005 and 2012 prizes as closed, because spectroscopy, laser cooling and trapping are close in method, and she asks that the citation emphasise neutral atoms trapped at the magic wavelength and interrogated in large ensembles.
responses.response: I accept that framing and I have adopted it: my citation now names the magic-wavelength trapping of neutral atoms, so the distinction from the comb and from single-ion control is written into the award and not argued afterwards. That answers the chair's first question for me. It does not make the overlap vanish, and I would not tell her to stop weighing it. I would only say that a citation which names the lattice as the invention is the strongest honest answer we can give, and I do not find the residual overlap disqualifying.

responses.point: Eriksson prefers B022 (Car and Parrinello) alone for its clean two-name credit and forty years of independent use, but names B030 as his first alternative and says he would not stand in the way of B030 on the merits.
responses.response: I respect his candour about field proximity and I agree the attribution of B022 is as clean as B030's. My difficulty is the one he raises himself: whether a computational method is a physics discovery or invention, and only two of eight members ranked it in the top eight. I would rather not decide that boundary question this year when a clean experimental invention with independent verification is available. I take his statement that he would defer on technical priority to Lindroth and Kroll as a sign that B030 can carry the committee, and I would welcome his support for it as the single prize part.

responses.point: Danielsson moved to B030 from B020, but lists as his reservation that this is an instrument achievement whose discovery content must be argued through tests of redshift, varying constants and dark matter, and he now accepts Spiering as the third name for B020.
responses.response: I agree that the discovery content has to be argued and I think Lindroth's light-shift, forbidden-transition and many-body reply makes that case: those are physics results, not packaging. On Spiering I now agree with him for a three-name B020, and that removes one of the two attribution differences between us. It does not remove the larger problem that the split among AMANDA founders, IceCube leaders and the collaboration is unsettled, which is why B020 stays my first alternative rather than my preferred prize. If we find ourselves choosing an astrophysics discovery, we should present Halzen, Karle and Spiering.

responses.point: Kroll holds B030 first on the Katori proposal plus Ye's record accuracy, would not tie it to the redefinition, and as an alternative lists B004, saying he would not defend his own trio against Bloch, Greiner and Zoller.
responses.response: I accept his reading of the attribution and his position on the redefinition, and I record that the case rests on demonstrated performance. On B004 I concede his point: my earlier dropping of Greiner is hard to defend against Danielsson's argument about the 2002 Mott transition and the gas microscope. If B030 were set aside I would support a B004 configuration of Bloch, Greiner and Zoller over my own earlier trio, which also leaves Esslinger out, and I would want the committee to say openly that this cut is a judgement.

responses.point: Olsson says the citation should name the lattice clock and not metrology generally, that Lemonde and others are contested rather than clearly excluded, and that the committee should not wait for the SI redefinition.
responses.response: I agree on the citation scope and on not waiting for the redefinition. On Lemonde I differ slightly: I do not think we can call him clearly excluded or clearly included from the supplied evidence. The proposal and the decisive realization at record accuracy are what identify Katori and Ye, and I would present the two-name allocation as our considered judgement, with the other groups acknowledged in the background text. I would not add a third name unless someone shows evidence beyond what we have, and I do not see anyone arguing for that.

uncertainties: Whether the one-sentence distinction from the 2005 comb and 2012 trapped-ion prizes satisfies Mehlig and those who hold the overlap concern, or whether it remains disqualifying for any of them.
Whether the omission of Lemonde, Lisdat, Ludlow and the ion-clock groups will be judged a serious attribution gap; I cannot verify the credit shares from the supplied text.
For B020, how credit divides among conception, construction and analysis across AMANDA and IceCube, including whether Spiering belongs; I have not independently verified the detailed history.
Whether metrology colleagues would see a prize before the redefinition of the second as premature, although I do not think it should delay the award.
statement.conflict_note: No specific conflict is apparent for B030, and I have no documented tie to Katori or Ye. My astroparticle work on PAMELA, Fermi-LAT, PoGOLite/PoGO+ and XL-Calibur makes me close to the subject of B020, with no recorded personal tie to its credited names; B020 is only my first alternative, and I flag this proximity without claiming a recusal-level conflict. As chair I see no recusal need for B030 on anyone's disclosure, and I note that B022, B029 and B025 raise disclosed proximity from Eriksson, Johansson and Olsson if they enter a configuration.
